_meta.model: MODELS.SMART; single call (was parallel split case+appeal) + groundedFacts pre-pass (ticket-appeal:{city}:{type}, 14d cache); followup 2000
_meta.how_to_regression_diff: Re-run (npm run check:golden ticket-tackler) — include the DE case. Diff for QUALITY not exact match: HTTP 200. GUARDS: (1) assessment.verdict and pay_or_contest.recommendation MUST be an exact English token WORTH_CONTESTING|VERIFY_FIRST|PROBABLY_PAY, and evidence_to_get[].urgency MUST be exactly today|before_filing — the frontend switches badge colors/labels on them; withLanguage would otherwise translate them in 12 langs. (2) NO numeric case-strength score and NO strength enum anywhere (2026-09-15 rewrite deliberately removed fight_worthiness and defense_angles[].strength — a 9/10 score or a strong/moderate/weak label implies predictive precision the tool does not have; do not reintroduce either). (3) pay_or_contest.reasoning must NEVER invent filing fees, hearing costs, preparation time, or a probability of success — the pre-rewrite decision_math routinely fabricated '20-30 minutes', '$10-20 reduction', 'roughly 15-30 minutes online'; the rewrite's reasoning weighs strength/evidence/amount-at-stake/procedural-burden in prose, with no invented numbers except the user-supplied fine amount. (4) appeal_letter MUST be null when there is no plausible supported basis for contesting (see weak-case) — do not always draft one 'to be helpful'; what_may_matter and what_to_verify MAY legitimately be empty arrays for a hopeless case — an empty array is a correct answer, not a broken response, so do not treat case-to-case count as an invariant the way non-empty arrays are. (5) dont_say MUST be null (not an empty array, not filler) unless the user's own account/wording actually contains something that could hurt their case. (6) how_to_file must NEVER invent portals/phones/deadlines: specifics come from the VERIFIED RULES block (grounding) or the response points to the ticket/official channel generically; deadline day-counts only if VERIFIED or user-provided. (7) what_may_matter items must be grounded in the user's account — no hypothetical stolen/leased-vehicle boilerplate, and each item distinguishes THE CITATION / THE USER'S ACCOUNT / SUPPORTING EVIDENCE / VERIFIED RULES rather than silently upgrading one into another (e.g. 'the sign as you describe it', not 'the sign'). (8) Quote-heavy German input → NO_QUOTE_RULE. (9) Statute sections cited only when certain (probe caught § 45 StVO cited slightly wrong in the pre-rewrite version — same caution applies to the rewritten prompt). DO NOT reverse: English enum pins; no numeric/categorical strength scoring anywhere; the grounded-or-generic how_to_file rule; the no-invented-decision-math rule; user-grounded what_may_matter; appeal_letter nullability; single-call architecture (letter drafting is now coupled to the assessment, so splitting it back into an unconditional parallel call would draft appeals for hopeless cases again — the exact bug this rewrite fixed).

input.ticketText:
CITY OF POCATELLO PARKING CITATION
Violation: EXPIRED METER (Code 10-24-2)
Location: 300 block N Main St
Date: 07/21/2026 Time: 2:14 PM
Fine: $25.00 - due within 14 days
Officer #217
input.whatHappened: ok so heres the thing. i parked on main st to run into the bank, put in two quarters but the meter screen was totally blank/dead - no time showing, no error, nothing. i figured it was broken so i left a note on my dash saying meter broken. came back like 25 min later and had a $25 expired meter ticket. i took a photo of the blank meter screen on my phone right then. this feels unfair, the meter literally ate my quarters and showed nothing

assessment.reason: As you describe it, a timestamped photo of a blank/dead meter screen taken minutes after the citation is contemporaneous evidence that the city's own equipment failed to register your payment — a factual basis distinct from simply disliking the fine.

what_may_matter.issue: Meter showed no time or error after payment was made
what_may_matter.supports_it: Your account is that you inserted two quarters and the screen stayed blank, and your photo (taken shortly after finding the citation) shows a blank display.
what_may_matter.needs_verification: Whether the photo's timestamp is close enough to the citation time to establish the meter was in that state when Officer #217 wrote the ticket, not only 25 minutes later when you returned.
what_may_matter.evidence_that_would_help: The photo's original file with metadata/timestamp intact, and, if obtainable, any city maintenance or complaint record for that meter around that date.

what_may_matter.issue: Note left on dashboard indicating the meter appeared broken
what_may_matter.supports_it: You report leaving a note before walking away, which is consistent with a good-faith attempt to pay rather than an attempt to avoid payment.
what_may_matter.needs_verification: Whether a photo or other record of the note exists, since the citation record alone won't show it.
what_may_matter.evidence_that_would_help: A photo of the note on the dashboard, ideally timestamped the same day.

what_to_verify: Whether Pocatello publishes a formal appeal deadline or process for parking citations — none was found in this search, so confirm directly with the issuing office.
Whether the meter at that location has any prior reported malfunctions on record.

evidence_to_get.item: The original photo file of the blank meter screen, with its timestamp preserved
evidence_to_get.why: This is the single fact the whole issue rests on — it needs to be clearly dated.

evidence_to_get.item: A photo of the note left on the dashboard, if one can still be taken or was already taken
evidence_to_get.why: Corroborates that you attempted to comply rather than skip payment.
Preserves the exact violation code, officer number, time, and location for reference in the appeal.

output.appeal_letter:
July 25, 2026

City of Pocatello Parking Violations
[CITATION #]

To Whom It May Concern,

I am requesting review and dismissal of Citation [CITATION #], issued July 21, 2026 at approximately 2:14 PM on the 300 block of N Main St for an alleged expired meter violation under Code 10-24-2.

When I parked, I inserted two quarters into the meter; the display remained blank, showing no time and no error. I left a note on my dashboard indicating the meter appeared broken, and returned approximately 25 minutes later to find the citation. I photographed the meter shortly afterward, and it still showed a blank screen.

I am enclosing that photograph. I respectfully request that this citation be dismissed on the basis that the meter did not register payment or display any time, which I believe indicates a malfunction rather than an expired term.

Thank you for your consideration.

[YOUR NAME]

how_to_file.where: No online contest portal was found for Pocatello parking citations as of this search — check the citation itself for a stated address or phone number, or contact the Pocatello Police Department directly.
how_to_file.method_tips: Attach a printed copy of your timestamped meter photo, and ask for a dated receipt or confirmation if submitting in person.
how_to_file.deadline_note: No official contest deadline was found for this jurisdiction — the citation states payment is due within 14 days, so contact the issuing office before that date to ask about the contest process and any separate deadline.

pay_or_contest.reasoning: The fine is small ($25), but the factual basis is concrete and rests on a single piece of contemporaneous photo evidence you already have — there's little to lose by raising it. The main friction is procedural: no published appeal process was found, so reaching the right office and confirming a deadline takes a direct call or visit rather than an online form.

dont_say: Avoid saying 'this feels unfair' — a hearing officer responds to the documented facts (the photo, the note), not to how the situation felt.

input.ticketText:
Stadt Schwäbisch Gmünd – Verwarnung
Tatvorwurf: Überschreiten der zulässigen Höchstparkdauer um 30 Minuten
Ort: Ledergasse, Bewohnerparkzone B
Verwarnungsgeld: 25,00 EUR
Zahlungsfrist: 1 Woche
input.whatHappened: Also, ich hab das Knöllchen an der Ledergasse bekommen. Der Kontrolleur meinte nur „Ihr Ausweis war nicht lesbar“ und ich hab gesagt „Der liegt doch da vorne!“. Mein Anwohnerparkausweis lag sichtbar auf dem Armaturenbrett, war aber wohl beim Türzuschlagen etwas verrutscht, sodass man ihn schräg von oben trotzdem sehen konnte. Angeblich hätte ich die Höchstparkdauer um 30 Minuten überschritten – aber als Anwohner mit Ausweis gilt die doch gar nicht für mich? Ich hab ein Foto vom Armaturenbrett mit dem Ausweis gemacht, direkt nachdem ich das Knöllchen gefunden hab.

assessment.reason: Als Inhaber eines gültigen Anwohnerparkausweises für Zone B gilt die Höchstparkdauer laut Ihrer Schilderung nicht für Sie, und Sie haben ein Foto, das den Ausweis sichtbar auf dem Armaturenbrett zeigt — ein klarer sachlicher Ansatzpunkt.

what_may_matter.issue: Anwohnerparkausweis befreit von der Höchstparkdauer in Zone B
what_may_matter.supports_it: Sie berichten, einen gültigen Ausweis für genau diese Zone zu besitzen — die zitierte Regel zur Höchstparkdauer träfe damit nicht zu.
what_may_matter.needs_verification: Dass der Ausweis zum Tatzeitpunkt tatsächlich gültig war (Datum, Kennzeichen, Zonenzuordnung B) — noch nicht durch etwas anderes als Ihre eigene Aussage belegt.
what_may_matter.evidence_that_would_help: Eine Kopie des Ausweises mit Gültigkeitsdauer, Kennzeichen und Zone.

what_may_matter.issue: Ausweis war sichtbar ausgelegt, nur verrutscht
what_may_matter.supports_it: Ihr Foto, unmittelbar nach dem Auffinden des Knöllchens aufgenommen, zeigt den Ausweis auf dem Armaturenbrett.
what_may_matter.needs_verification: Ob das Foto den Zustand zum Kontrollzeitpunkt widerspiegelt und nicht erst danach verändert wurde.
what_may_matter.evidence_that_would_help: Das Foto selbst mit Zeitstempel/EXIF-Daten, falls vorhanden.

what_to_verify: Der genaue Wortlaut der Zonenregelung für Bewohnerparkzone B — ob Anwohner tatsächlich vollständig von der Höchstparkdauer ausgenommen sind oder nur bestimmte Bedingungen gelten.
Die formale Widerspruchsfrist und das zuständige Amt, falls von der Stadt Schwäbisch Gmünd nicht bereits auf dem Knöllchen angegeben.

evidence_to_get.item: Foto vom Armaturenbrett mit Ausweis sichern (Original mit Zeitstempel)
evidence_to_get.why: Belegt, dass der Ausweis sichtbar ausgelegt war.

evidence_to_get.item: Anwohnerparkausweis fotografieren oder einscannen (Vorder- und Rückseite)

evidence_to_get.why: Enthält Aktenzeichen und Tatvorwurf für die Eingabe bei der Bußgeldstelle.

output.appeal_letter:
Schwäbisch Gmünd, [DATUM]

Stadt Schwäbisch Gmünd
Rechts- und Ordnungsamt / Bußgeldstelle
Waisenhausgasse 1–3
73525 Schwäbisch Gmünd

Betreff: Widerspruch zur Verwarnung – Aktenzeichen [CITATION #]

Sehr geehrte Damen und Herren,

hiermit widerspreche ich der oben genannten Verwarnung vom [DATUM DES KNÖLLCHENS] über 25,00 EUR wegen angeblicher Überschreitung der Höchstparkdauer in der Ledergasse, Bewohnerparkzone B.

Ein unmittelbar nach Vorfinden des Verwarnungszettels aufgenommenes Foto belege ich als Anlage.

Ich bitte um Prüfung und Einstellung des Verfahrens.

Mit freundlichen Grüßen

how_to_file.where: Schriftlich einreichen bei: Stadt Schwäbisch Gmünd, Rechts- und Ordnungsamt / Bußgeldstelle, Waisenhausgasse 1–3, 73525 Schwäbisch Gmünd — bestätigen Sie diese Adresse anhand des Knöllchens selbst.
how_to_file.method_tips: Per Einschreiben mit Rückschein senden, um den Eingang nachweisen zu können; Foto und Ausweiskopie beilegen.
how_to_file.deadline_note: Das Verwarnungsgeld ist laut Ticket binnen einer Woche fällig — prüfen Sie das genaue Ausstellungsdatum auf dem Knöllchen, um die Frist korrekt zu berechnen.

pay_or_contest.reasoning: Die Ausnahme für Anwohner mit gültigem Ausweis ist ein konkreter sachlicher Punkt, kein vager Einwand, und ein Foto stützt ihn bereits. Der Betrag ist gering, aber der Widerspruch beruht auf einer einzigen, klaren Tatsache statt auf einer rechtlichen Interpretation.

dont_say: Vermeiden Sie die Aussage 'Der Kontrolleur war unfreundlich' — persönliche Kritik lenkt vom sachlichen Punkt ab und wirkt nicht zu Ihren Gunsten.

input.whatHappened: Honestly I knew better. I parked directly in a no-parking zone on SE Division - the sign is big, red, totally unobstructed, right next to my car. I was only there like 5 minutes to grab a coffee and came back to a $40 ticket. I even took a photo of the sign and yeah, it's completely clear and unambiguous. No permit, no loading, I just risked it. Is there any angle here or do I just eat it?

assessment.reason: By your own account the sign was clear, unobstructed, and unambiguous, you had no permit, and you confirmed this with your own photo — there is no factual inconsistency to raise, and a sympathetic explanation ('just 5 minutes') is not a defense.

evidence_to_get.item: The citation itself, noting the exact issue date
evidence_to_get.why: Confirms the exact deadline for any response, in case you want to pay online before it becomes delinquent.

how_to_file.where: Check the citation for the payment address or online portal, or the Multnomah County Circuit Court's parking page for Portland citations.
how_to_file.method_tips: If paying online, keep the payment confirmation; if by mail, keep a copy of what you sent.
how_to_file.deadline_note: The citation should state a specific response window — verify the exact date printed on it rather than assuming a standard number of days.

pay_or_contest.reasoning: You've confirmed the sign was clear and unobstructed and that no permit or loading exception applied — there's no factual dispute with the citation and nothing supplied that would support contesting it. Paying resolves it without the risk of a missed deadline or additional fees.

dont_say: Avoid saying 'I was only there five minutes' — duration isn't a defense to this kind of violation and only draws attention to the fact that you deliberately risked it.

input.ticketText:
CITY OF CHICAGO - DEPARTMENT OF FINANCE
AUTOMATED RED LIGHT CAMERA VIOLATION
Location: Western Ave & Peterson Ave
Date: 07/18/2026 9:42 PM
Violation: Disobeying a red light
Penalty: $100.00
Two photographs and video available online
input.whatHappened: I got a red light camera ticket at Western and Peterson. Here's the thing - I entered the intersection on yellow, I was already past the stop line and mid-intersection when it flipped to red. The yellow felt really short at that intersection, like it barely gave me time to react at 35mph. The photos show my car in the middle of the intersection. $100 seems steep for this. Worth fighting?

assessment.reason: Entering on yellow and being mid-intersection when the light turned red does not, by itself, contest what the camera measures — but it's worth checking whether an officer separately issued a paper citation for the same incident, which some cities treat as grounds for dismissal, before deciding to pay.

what_to_verify: Whether a Chicago Police officer issued a separate, hand-written traffic citation for this same incident — if one exists, it may be grounds for dismissal under the city's own camera-violation rules.
What the two photographs and video actually show — specifically whether your vehicle had already crossed the stop line before or after the signal turned red, which is the fact the citation turns on.

evidence_to_get.item: Review the two photos and video available online using the citation number
evidence_to_get.why: Establishes, from the city's own evidence, whether your vehicle crossed the stop line before or after the light turned red — the fact the case turns on.

evidence_to_get.item: Check your records for any hand-written police citation from the night of 07/18/2026
evidence_to_get.why: A duplicate citation for the same incident is a distinct, checkable fact that could change the answer entirely.

how_to_file.where: Contest online via the city's eContest portal at parkingtickets.chicago.gov, or by mail or in person at a City of Chicago hearing facility.
how_to_file.method_tips: The online system lets you request a virtual, correspondence, or in-person hearing.
how_to_file.deadline_note: Citations of this kind typically state a response window from the Notice of Violation date — confirm the exact deadline printed on your notice before doing anything else.

pay_or_contest.reasoning: The argument you have — that you entered on yellow — addresses your own intent, not the fact the camera measures (where your vehicle was when the light turned red), so it's unlikely to change the outcome on its own. The one thing worth confirming before paying is whether a duplicate paper citation exists, since that's a distinct, checkable fact rather than an interpretation.

dont_say: Avoid leading with 'the yellow felt too short' — this describes your reaction to the signal timing, not a fact the citation or a hearing officer can act on.

input.question: What if I just don't pay it?
input.analysisContext: PROBABLY_PAY: User admittedly parked in a clearly-marked, unobstructed no-parking zone on SE Division for 5 minutes; $40 fine; own photo confirms the sign. No basis for an appeal was found.

output.answer: Not paying will not make the ticket go away. Portland sends unpaid parking tickets to collections, adds late fees, and can place a hold on your vehicle registration renewal with the Oregon DMV. For a $40 ticket you've confirmed you owe, non-payment is the most expensive option available to you.
output.watch_out: Oregon DMV registration holds are a real enforcement mechanism — you won't be able to renew your plates until the debt is resolved.
output.next_step: Pay the $40 through the method listed on the ticket itself before the deadline printed on it.
